body.statement: When \(S=\varnothing\), CIDP exchanges only nonempty intersections of the current treatment or conditioning set with a bucket, and only when the corresponding PAG Rule--2 separation holds.  On success it reaches a role state \(\rho_\star=(\bar X_\star,\bar C_\star)\), identifies \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y,\bar C_\star\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X_\star))\) by its marginal algorithm, and normalizes that joint functional.  CIDP is sound and complete for identification of \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X),C)\) from an input-free PAG.

source.verbatim_statement: Algorithm 2 CIDP(P,x,y,z) moves bucket intersections between intervention and conditioning only after the displayed Rule 2 separation tests, then calls IDP(P,x,y union z) and returns E divided by the sum over y-prime of E. Theorem 4 (completeness). Alg. 2 is complete for identifying conditional effects P_x(y|z). Also, the calculus in Thm. 1, together with standard probability manipulations are complete for the same task.
